title: Strong transcendence passes to the quotient by a minimal prime
statement: Let $R\subseteq S$ be a subring of a commutative ring, with $R$ and $S$ reduced (no nonzero nilpotent elements), and let $x\in S$ be strongly transcendental over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strongly-transcendental] (for the inclusion $R\to S$). Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a minimal prime ideal of $S$ (a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime ideal) and $\mathfrak p=R\cap\mathfrak q$. Then the image $\bar x$ of $x$ in $S/\mathfrak q$ is strongly transcendental over $R/\mathfrak p$ for the ring map $R/\mathfrak p\to S/\mathfrak q$ induced by the inclusion: if $\bar u(\bar a_0+\bar a_1\bar x+\dots+\bar a_k\bar x^k)=0$ in $S/\mathfrak q$ with $\bar u\in S/\mathfrak q$ and $\bar a_i\in R/\mathfrak p$, then $\bar u\bar a_i=0$ for all $i$.
